chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Hearing Charlie Parker for the first time
summary: He first heard Charlie Parker blowing at a club near the Monroe Inn after Bird's woodshedding in the Ozarks; Bird later went to New York and saw the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Gene had been with her. But at this time, I got Gene, so that worked out good. And then I made a few changes and I got Willie Scott in the band. And let's see, Popeye left the band. After Popeye left the band, then I got Yardbird. So I had Yardbird --
Well, where did you hear him?
Well, the first time I heard Bird was when I was working out to the Monroe Inn with Hop

and I thought I had met most of the musicians in Kansas City, but I happened to be coming through the street on this particular night, you know, and you know how they would pipe the music outside? Cats be blowing in the mike? And you would hear it out in front?

Loudspeaker. And so, I was walking across the street and I heard this sound. I said, "Oh, wait a minute. I haven't heard this cat before." So I decided to go in and see who it was. So I went in there and listened to him blow. After they finished playing, I walked up to him, said, "Hey, man, I haven't met you. I've met most of the cats, but where have you been?" He said, "Well, I've been down in Ozarks with George Lee's band. You know, it's hard to get musicians to go down to the Ozarks because it's so quiet down there. So I figured I wanted to do some woodshedding and so that's why I went." I said, "Well, man, you play different from anybody around Kansas City." He said, "Well, I've been down there woodshedding, you see. That's what's been happening." And that was our first meeting.
What year would this be? '37 or '38?

It's '37, '37, because he came to work with me in '38. See, he worked with the small group there for about four or five months and then he decided, he said, "Man, I want to go see New York. I'm just going up there. I want to

see it." And that's when he went -- you know, just went on a trip, stopped in Chicago and went on to New York and he was telling me about how he stood out there and looked at the sign that said Savoy Ballroom. He looked at the marquee and how thrilled he was. He told me about that after he came back. He said, "Man, that Savoy, just thrilled as I could be. Just standing there, looking at the marquee and just looking at everything," you know. And he came on back to Kansas City. He came back to Kansas City, he started working with Harlan Leonard's band. So he was working with Harlan's band and so by this time, you see, I've got a big band started.
